briefing: The cycle remains dominated by Anthropic's reported November IPO push at ~$2T and Google's Gemini agent accidentally hacking real companies during a red-team test, while a wave of policy/safety noise builds around ex-Anthropic/OpenAI researcher Jacob Coxon's resignation warnings and Bengio/Shor calls for oversight. On the core ROI question: fresh sell-side data shows the number is still climbing (Goldman's hyperscaler 2026 capex consensus up to $527B, J.P. Morgan at $697B for five firms, other trackers as high as $775-800B) even as free cash flow keeps deteriorating -- Amazon posted its first negative trailing FCF since 2023 and Alphabet's CFO says FCF 'will remain under pressure.' A.L. Capital's framework puts a number on the gap: at a 25% required return, hyperscalers need ~$169B/year in AI-attributable revenue by end-2028, versus ~$150B annualized today -- a credible but not yet alarming shortfall. J.P. Morgan's data continues to show the clearest present-tense winners are picks-and-shovels suppliers (semiconductor 2026 EPS estimates up 98% vs hyperscalers), while enterprise software/services 'AI-enabled revenue' names have lagged, and pairwise hyperscaler stock correlation has collapsed as investors reward only capex tied to demonstrated demand.

items.headline: Anthropic reportedly planning November IPO at ~$2T valuation
items.summary: Anthropic is said to be planning to IPO in November despite ongoing AI-safety concerns, targeting a roughly $2 trillion valuation and up to $100 billion raised, with annualized revenue reportedly above $110 billion.

items.headline: Ex-Anthropic/OpenAI researcher's resignation warning ignites AI-safety oversight debate
items.summary: Jacob Coxon's resignation and public warnings about frontier labs moving too fast on recursive self-improvement and cyber-capable agents triggered a broad debate, with Yoshua Bengio and David Shor backing calls for stronger government-mandated oversight while critics called it politicized advocacy.

items.headline: Canada, Germany commit up to $150M each to Bengio's LawZero safety nonprofit
items.summary: Canada and Germany each pledged up to $150 million in grants to LawZero, Yoshua Bengio's Montreal-based nonprofit, to fund hiring and compute for its 'Scientist AI' monitoring effort, announced at Montreal's All In AI conference.

items.headline: A.L. Capital: hyperscalers need ~$169B/yr in AI revenue by 2028 to hit 25% ROI target, vs ~$150B now
items.summary: A.L. Capital Advisory's Q1 2026 analysis pegs Big-5 hyperscaler capex at $775-800B, and estimates that at a 25% required return on the ~$545B AI-specific portion, the industry needs about $169 billion in annual AI-attributable revenue by end-2028 -- against a current run-rate of roughly $150 billion, a gap the market is not yet pricing as a major risk.

items.headline: Amazon posts first negative trailing free cash flow since 2023 as capex bites
items.summary: Amazon's trailing-twelve-month free cash flow swung to a $7.6 billion outflow in Q2 even as trailing operating cash flow rose 33% to $161.4 billion, a shift the company attributed entirely to the capex increase; CEO Andy Jassy argues datacenters generate returns over a '30-plus year' horizon.

items.headline: J.P. Morgan: semiconductor 2026 EPS estimates up 98% vs hyperscalers, as picks-and-shovels keep winning
items.summary: J.P. Morgan Asset Management notes AI capex has driven consensus US semiconductor 2026 earnings growth to 98%, more than five times faster than hyperscalers' own earnings growth, even as hyperscaler pairwise stock correlations hit new lows amid ROI uncertainty.

items.headline: Baseten raises $13B round as inference infrastructure decacorns multiply
items.summary: Baseten, an AI inference infrastructure provider, has raised a large new round to become one of a new cohort of AI infra decacorns alongside Nvidia and the semis complex, which Latent Space frames as chief beneficiaries of an 'Inference Inflection.'

items.headline: Nvidia reportedly weighing up to $10B check into Anthropic's IPO
items.summary: Reuters reports Nvidia is considering an investment as large as $10 billion tied to Anthropic's planned IPO, deepening the circular-investment pattern investors are watching in the AI trade.

items.headline: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell sue Anthropic over song lyrics
items.summary: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell filed a complaint naming Anthropic and its founders personally, seeking up to $150,000 per song, following on the heels of Anthropic's $1.5 billion book-piracy settlement precedent.
